task_retrieval_key: A 21-month-old male presented to the emergency department with respiratory symptoms. Over the past 10 months, there has been a noted increase in penile size and skin darkening. A sibling passed away 13 years ago with similar symptoms. The patient's weight was 13 kg (Z-score: 1.1, 85.3th percentile), height was 92 cm (Z-score: 2.4, 99.2th percentile), and blood pressure was 139/90 mmHg (Z-score for age-based pediatric blood pressure for systolic/diastolic pressure: 4.3/3.9, 100th percentile. Z-score equal to or greater than 95th percentile indicates hypertension). Physical examination revealed hyperpigmentation of the gums, skin, and scrotum, facial acne, and penile enlargement measuring 8.7 cm (above 90th percentile). Testicular size was prepubertal (less than 2 mL) with no pubic hair.
